136: Skill RT Formula (base + weapon WT) × SkillMult

USER RULING 2026-10-04 - SUPERSEDES the old weapon-WT-only skill RT model. FORMULA: Skill RT = round((Modified Base RT × 0.10 + Effective Weapon WT) × SkillMult). 'Modified Base RT × 0.10' is the SAME base component used by Basic Attack RT (Basic Attack RT = round(Modified Base RT × 0.10) + Effective Weapon WT); skills previously lacked it. Effective Weapon WT = raw weapon WT × (1 − STR/(200+STR)), same as Basic Attack. SkillMult = the per-skill N stored in skills.RT_Cost_Formula; N scales the WHOLE cost (base component + Effective Weapon WT), not just the weapon-WT term (confirmed by user 2026-10-04). RATIONALE (user): skill RT should derive from Basic Attack RT (which includes the Modified-Base-RT base component) plus weapon WT, so skills are indirectly affected by Modified Base RT just like basic attacks; the whole basic-attack-equivalent cost is then scaled by the skill's weight. SCOPE: applies ONLY to skills whose formula was round(Effective Weapon WT × N). FIXED / level-based RT skills (e.g. SKL-RAINFALL-ZONE round(70 + 0.30L), SKL-BLINK round(40 + 0.20L), SKL-PHANTOM-EXCHANGE round(60 + 0.35L), SKL-STEAL, the L-based doctrine skills) keep their authored formula unchanged. Twinblade skills (Dual-Wield Basic Attack RT based) also unchanged. LAYERS AFTER (unchanged): Frozen ×2 (GetAllRtMultiplier) and Arcane Prodigy trait Skill RT Cost multiplier (perk ×0.92 / flaw ×1.08) apply on top of the new Skill RT; doctrine/augment Skill-RT-Cost modifiers (Tactician -10%, Trickster -25%, Shieldbearer -25%, Shared Resolve ×2) likewise apply to the new value. WORKED EXAMPLES (Modified Base RT 400 -> base component 40; Effective Weapon WT 30): Fire Bolt N=1.00 -> round((40+30)×1.00) = 70 (old 30). Meteor Marker N=1.40 -> round((40+30)×1.40) = 98 (old 42). EFFECT: every weapon-WT-based skill costs more RT (gains ~40×N). Intended, game-wide.

4: Quick one-charge Items buy tempo. Multi-charge Items provide endurance at higher RT. Major weather, terrain, deployable, revival, and delayed-burst Items use one or two charges and heavier RT.
5: All values are working baselines. They are designed to be plausible battle options, but still require simulation against Basic Attacks, Skills, encounter length, and base-return frequency.
6: For Items with one or two charges, AI preserves the final charge unless the action prevents probable defeat, secures a major objective, or produces decisive tactical value.
15: Standard unit Base RT = 400. Default Item RT is 40 before a specific Item overrides it. Item RT must remain competitive with authored Skill RT rather than behaving like an additional full turn.
16: 45–85 RT, usually 1 charge. Emergency healing, MP recovery, escape, immediate cleanse, or narrow tactical setup.
17: 70–95 RT, usually 4–5 charges. Narrow utility, basic buffs/debuffs, simple damage, reveal, repair, or terrain preparation.
18: 90–120 RT, usually 3 charges. Medium healing, meaningful control, AOE damage, movement tools, and ordinary deployables.
19: 130–165 RT, usually 1–2 charges. Revival, strong AOE/control, walls, high-impact summons, large healing, or major terrain changes.
20: 180–220 RT, 1 charge. Weather, siege, major path creation, encounter-shaping deployables, and visible delayed burst.
21: Items gain breadth from universal access but normally remain less efficient than specialized Skills. They do not use MP, Skill slots, or Augments, so charges and RT must carry real opportunity cost.
30: Shop Price = round(Base Profile Price × Tier Multiplier / 5) × 5. Rounded to nearest 5g.
33: 25g (Common Quick) to 480g (Epic Battlefield). Average ~171g across catalog. Median 220g.
35: Common items = 1/6 to 1/2 of a battle. Always affordable. Rare Heavy = 3/4 of a battle. Meaningful choice. Epic Battlefield = 1-2 battles. Luxury.
